propositions: Multiple bundles for a single ref on S3 cause ref ambiguity, clone failure with 'multiple updates for ref not allowed', and push stall when git-remote-s3 rejects writes while bundles>1 before creating any bundle

Upstream's git-remote-s3 Doctor.fix_multiple_bundles is interactive-only (blocking input() on EOF) and discards non-chosen heads, causing permanent data loss of unique ticket events in an append-only store

The heal must never discard heads; it must losslessly merge all divergent bundle tips via iterated 2-parent merges (not octopus, not merge=union), reusing rebar's existing sync._union_merge semantics and .gitattributes merge=ours for .bridge_state/*

The heal acquires git-remote-s3's per-ref lock, re-enumerates bundles under the lock, fetches all heads locally, folds them via write_lock-scoped merges, writes the merged tip as a new bundle before deleting originals, and deletes no bundle after the merge is written (crash-safe ordering: >=1 lossless bundle always present)

All S3 access (lock, enumerate, list, delete) routes through git-remote-s3's own S3Remote/.s3 client imported lazily behind require_s3_helper(), adding no direct boto3 dependency to core rebar and no reinvented lock/credential/key-layout code
push_tickets_branch detects the multi-bundle signature, invokes heal_multi_bundle exactly once (guarded by healed_once), then retries the push, converging without infinite non-FF loops
